sources.title: Russell W. Howell and John H. Mathews, Complex Analysis, Section 8.7 The Argument Principle and Rouché's Theorem
sources.locator: Section 8.7, including Definition 8.7.1, Theorem 8.7.2, Corollary 8.7.3, Remark 8.7.4, Theorem 8.7.9, Remark 8.7.10, Theorem 8.7.11, Corollary 8.7.12, Remark 8.7.13, and Examples 8.7.7, 8.7.14, 8.7.15.

contents.name: Remark 8.7.4.
contents.reason: The Nyquist stability application is a legitimate application of the argument principle, but this page keeps the pure complex-analysis spine and does not open a control-theory branch.

contents.name: Remark 8.7.13.
contents.reason: The design explicitly declines the stronger symmetric Glicksberg form of Rouché. The page keeps the classical strict-dominance theorem only.

contents.name: Example 8.7.7.
contents.reason: The page keeps a winding-number example, but not this exact quadratic image-curve computation. The scaffold uses a cubic example so the quadratic worked example is not minted separately.

contents.name: Example 8.7.14.
contents.reason: The worked Rouché example is mathematically standard, but the design's B page already chooses different zero-count examples and this one does not feed any later dependency.

contents.name: Example 8.7.15.
contents.reason: This is another standard Rouché counting exercise, but the designed companion page uses the z^5+3z+1 and e^z=3z examples instead.

Exercise 5.4.2.
contents.reason: This localization exercise supports the proof housekeeping around finitely many relevant zeros and poles, but the scaffold uses the already-published finiteness lemmas from the winding-number and residue pages instead of minting a duplicate helper.

contents.name: Exercise 5.4.3.
contents.reason: This is a worked integral computation with the argument principle. The designed companion page uses different applications and does not need this exact exercise as a scaffold item.

contents.name: Exercise 2.6.2.
